feature.title: Automated Railway Deployment via GitHub Actions for Customer Support AI Chatbot
feature.description: Provide a GitHub Actions–driven deployment pipeline that automatically builds and deploys the Customer Support AI Chatbot to Railway, producing an isolated running copy per environment (Development, Testing, Production) with a public URL. This feature removes the need for manual deployments by triggering a deployment when code is pushed or merged into configured branches. Assumptions: (1) the repository contains a buildable application that Railway can run; (2) branch-to-environment mapping will be: main -> Production, develop -> Development, testing -> Testing; (3) a Railway API token is stored in the repository as a GitHub secret (e.g., RAILWAY_TOKEN); (4) the running app responds with HTTP 200 at the root path (/) to indicate a healthy deployment.
feature.business_value: Automating deployment to Railway via GitHub Actions increases release velocity, reduces human error from manual deployment steps, and ensures each environment (Development/Testing/Production) has an isolated, reproducible running copy of the Customer Support AI Chatbot with a public URL for testing and production use.

acceptance_criteria.given: A GitHub repository for the chatbot with a GitHub Actions workflow configured to deploy to Railway and a Railway project created; the RAILWAY_TOKEN secret is set in the repository; the branch-to-environment mapping is configured as main -> Production.
acceptance_criteria.when: When a commit is merged into the main branch, Then the GitHub Actions workflow starts, completes successfully, and a Railway deployment is created or updated for the Production environment; the workflow log contains a Railway deployment success message and the deployment metadata includes a public URL.

acceptance_criteria.given: The same GitHub repository and workflow as above and branch-to-environment mapping configured (develop -> Development).
acceptance_criteria.when: When a commit is pushed to the develop branch, Then the GitHub Actions workflow starts, completes successfully, and a Railway deployment is created or updated for the Development environment; the Production environment deployment is not modified by this action; the workflow log contains the Development deployment public URL.

acceptance_criteria.given: An existing successful Production deployment timestamp and an existing Development deployment timestamp prior to a new Development deployment.
acceptance_criteria.when: When a new deployment is triggered for the Development environment (e.g., push to develop), Then the Development environment's deployment timestamp is updated while the Production environment's deployment timestamp remains unchanged, demonstrating environment isolation.

acceptance_criteria.given: The repository has the RAILWAY_TOKEN stored as a GitHub secret and the workflow references that secret for Railway authentication.
acceptance_criteria.when: When the GitHub Actions workflow runs to deploy, Then the workflow authenticates to Railway using the secret (authentication success is visible in logs or deployment metadata) and the token value does not appear in plaintext anywhere in the workflow logs.

acceptance_criteria.given: A commit that causes a build error (for example, an intentional syntax error) is pushed to the branch that triggers a deployment.
acceptance_criteria.when: When the GitHub Actions workflow runs for that commit, Then the workflow fails (job marked failed), the Railway deployment for that environment is not updated, and the GitHub Actions run is marked with a failing status visible in the repository's Actions tab and on the commit/PR status.

acceptance_criteria.given: A successful Railway deployment has returned a public URL for the deployed environment and the application is assumed to serve an HTTP 200 at the root path (/).
acceptance_criteria.when: When the returned public URL is requested via HTTP GET to '/', Then the response returns HTTP 200 within an acceptable timeout (e.g., 10 seconds), indicating the deployed chatbot instance is responding.
